purpose: Inclisiran is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL cholesterol) in adults when diet and other cholesterol-lowering medicines like statins are not enough. It is used in people with a genetic condition that causes very high cholesterol or in those who have had heart disease such as a heart attack or stroke. Keeping LDL cholesterol low helps protect your heart and blood vessels.
how_it_works: Your liver makes a protein called PCSK9 that breaks down the receptors responsible for removing bad cholesterol from your blood. Inclisiran works by blocking the genetic instructions inside liver cells that tell your body to make PCSK9. With less PCSK9 being made, more cholesterol-clearing receptors stay active, so your liver can pull more bad cholesterol out of your bloodstream and lower your levels.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is mild reactions at the injection site such as redness, pain, bruising, or swelling where the shot was given. Some people may also notice mild joint pain or a urinary tract infection. These effects are generally mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine in pregnancy is not fully known. Always let all of your healthcare providers know every medicine and supplement you are taking. This medicine is given by a healthcare provider as an injection under the skin, so do not try to inject it yourself at home unless specifically instructed and trained to do so.
typical_dosing: Inclisiran is given as an injection under the skin by a healthcare provider, usually in a clinic or doctor's office. You get the first dose, then a second dose 3 months later, and after that just two doses per year — roughly every 6 months. This convenient schedule means you only need two shots a year to help keep your cholesterol under control.
